documents.title: Psychiatric Admission Evaluation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
WESTMERE REGIONAL HOSPITAL, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH UNIT
Psychiatric Admission Evaluation
Date of admission: 06/09/2026

Patient: Tyler Boucher, 34-year-old man

Reason for admission: inpatient stabilization of psychotic symptoms.

History of present illness: Over roughly the past 8 months Mr. Boucher has been hearing voices that others do not hear. His speech has become increasingly disorganized and difficult to follow, and he has withdrawn from the people around him. No prior psychiatric treatment or hospitalization.

Psychiatric history: none prior.
Medical history: alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (PiZZ) with emphysema; mitochondrial myopathy; seasonal allergic rhinitis on subcutaneous immunotherapy; exercise intolerance.
Surgical: tonsillectomy.
Home medications: cetirizine 10 mg daily as needed; fluticasone propionate nasal spray 2 sprays per nostril daily; monthly allergen immunotherapy (outside); albuterol HFA 2 puffs every 4 to 6 hours as needed; alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor (human) 60 mg/kg IV weekly by home infusion (pulmonology).
Allergies: tree, grass and weed pollen. No known drug allergies.
Family history: maternal uncle with schizophrenia. Identical twin brother, well, with no psychiatric illness; he has been in touch with the team and has asked about his own chances of developing a similar illness. Mother has mitochondrial myopathy. Father, now deceased, had alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.
Social history: freelance graphic designer. Never smoker. Alcohol socially, 1-2 drinks per week. Denies recreational drug use.

Mental status examination: Alert and cooperative. Speech disorganized and at times hard to follow. Reports auditory hallucinations. Socially withdrawn on the unit. Denies suicidal or homicidal ideation. Oriented to person, place and time.

Assessment: Symptoms meet DSM-5 criteria for schizophrenia.

Plan:
1. Admit to the behavioral health unit for stabilization.
2. Start risperidone 2 mg by mouth daily.
3. Start benztropine 1 mg by mouth twice daily.
4. Continue cetirizine, fluticasone and albuterol as needed. Hold the weekly augmentation infusions during the admission; resume at home after discharge.
5. Social work and family meeting; team to meet with his brother regarding his question.

Attending Psychiatrist, Behavioral Health Unit

documents.title: Psychiatric Discharge Summary
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
WESTMERE REGIONAL HOSPITAL, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH UNIT
Discharge Summary

Patient: Tyler Boucher, DOB 07/29/1991
Admitted: 06/09/2026  Discharged: 06/26/2026

Discharge diagnosis: Schizophrenia.
Other diagnoses: alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with emphysema; mitochondrial myopathy; seasonal allergic rhinitis.

Hospital course: Admitted for stabilization after about eight months of auditory hallucinations, disorganized speech and social withdrawal; DSM-5 criteria for schizophrenia met. Started on risperidone 2 mg daily with benztropine 1 mg twice daily. Psychotic symptoms improved over the stay on risperidone. He was judged ready for discharge home with outpatient follow-up.

Family: During the admission his identical twin brother, who is well, asked the team about his own risk of developing schizophrenia. He was told that his risk is higher than that of the general population; no specific figures were given.

Discharge medications:
- Risperidone 2 mg by mouth daily (new)
- Benztropine 1 mg by mouth twice daily (new)
- Cetirizine 10 mg by mouth daily as needed (continued)
- Fluticasone propionate 50 mcg nasal spray, 2 sprays per nostril once daily (continued)
- Allergen immunotherapy injections, monthly at allergist (continued)
- Albuterol HFA 90 mcg, 2 puffs every 4 to 6 hours as needed (continued)
- Alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor (human) 60 mg/kg IV weekly by home infusion (held during the admission; resume)
Allergies: tree, grass and weed pollen. No known drug allergies.

Follow-up: outpatient psychiatry appointment arranged; details given to patient. PCP within 1 to 2 weeks.

Attending Psychiatrist, Behavioral Health Unit

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
WESTMERE REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Provider note, arrival 07/03/2026 14:25 (Friday)

CC: confusion

HPI: 34-year-old man, discharged from our behavioral health unit one week ago with a new diagnosis of schizophrenia, started there on risperidone 2 mg daily and benztropine 1 mg twice daily. Also has alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency and mitochondrial myopathy. For the last two days he has been confused and restless, eating and drinking very little, and complains his vision is blurry. His roommate, who brought him, says he has been behaving strangely, talking to himself, and will not eat or drink. The patient says he feels much too hot. History limited by his mental status; obtained from roommate and our discharge records.

Meds (per discharge list): risperidone 2 mg daily; benztropine 1 mg BID; cetirizine 10 mg PRN; fluticasone nasal; monthly allergen immunotherapy; albuterol PRN; alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor IV weekly by home infusion.
Allergies on arrival: tree/grass/weed pollen; no drug allergies.
PMH: schizophrenia (06/2026), AATD (PiZZ) with emphysema, mitochondrial myopathy, allergic rhinitis.

Exam:
T 38.1 C (100.6 F), HR 104, BP 152/88, RR 18, SpO2 95% RA.
General: restless, not in respiratory distress.
Skin: flushed, warm and dry. No rash.
HEENT: mucous membranes dry. Pupils 5 mm bilaterally, sluggishly reactive to light.
Neck: supple.
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur.
Lungs: clear, no crackles.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, bladder not palpable.
Neuro: no rigidity, no clonus, no tremor. Moves all extremities. Inattentive; disoriented to time and place.

Workup:
- CBC: within normal limits.
- BMP: within normal limits.
- CK 549 U/L; near his chronic baseline in the 500s with known mitochondrial myopathy.
- Urinalysis: unremarkable.

MDM: Delirium with fever, tachycardia, hypertension, flushed dry skin, dry mucosa, mydriasis and blurred vision, one week after starting benztropine: anticholinergic toxicity from benztropine. No rigidity and CK at his baseline make neuroleptic malignant syndrome unlikely. Labs otherwise reassuring.

ED course: benztropine held. IV normal saline. Cooling measures and a low-stimulation room. Placed in observation for serial reassessment.

Diagnosis: Adverse effect of anticholinergic medication (benztropine) with delirium.
Benztropine discontinued. Benztropine (anticholinergic toxicity) entered as a drug allergy.

Emergency Medicine Attending
cc: PCP

documents.title: ED Observation Discharge
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
WESTMERE REGIONAL HOSPITAL, ED Observation Unit
Discharge note, 07/04/2026 11:30

Observed overnight on IV fluids and supportive care for benztropine anticholinergic toxicity. Temperature down by evening. By the morning of 07/04: afebrile (T 37.0), HR 84, BP 124/78, SpO2 95%. Alert, calm and oriented to person, place and time. Eating and drinking. Pupils normal size and reactive. Vision clear per patient.

Disposition: discharged home with his roommate.

Medication changes: STOP benztropine. Other home medications unchanged.
New allergy: Benztropine (anticholinergic toxicity).

Communication: our inpatient psychiatry team was informed of the visit and the benztropine reaction before discharge.

Follow-up: outpatient psychiatry as scheduled; PCP in 1 to 2 weeks. Return for fever, confusion, stiffness or inability to eat or drink.

ED Observation Physician

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit after psychiatric admission and ED observation stay.

Timeline from outside records:
- 6/9 to 6/26 Westmere Regional BHU: schizophrenia diagnosed (about 8 months of symptoms), started risperidone 2 mg daily and benztropine 1 mg BID, improved, discharged with outpatient psychiatry follow-up.
- 7/3 to 7/4 Westmere ED/obs: two days of confusion, restlessness, poor intake, blurred vision; febrile 38.1, HR 104, BP 152/88, flushed dry skin, dilated sluggish pupils, no rigidity. CBC, BMP, UA normal; CK 549 (his usual). Anticholinergic toxicity from benztropine. IV fluids, observed overnight, afebrile and oriented next morning. Benztropine stopped and added as an allergy.

Today: Tyler says he feels like himself again since getting out of the ED, no fevers, eating and drinking normally, vision is fine. Taking risperidone every day, no benztropine since 7/3. Outpatient psychiatry is following him and he has seen them since discharge. Still on cetirizine, fluticasone and monthly allergy shots. Weekly augmentation infusions were held during the admission and restarted at home on 7/2; albuterol now and then.

Meds: risperidone 2 mg daily; cetirizine 10 mg PRN; fluticasone nasal 2 sprays each nostril daily; SCIT monthly (outside); albuterol HFA PRN; alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor 60 mg/kg IV weekly (home infusion, pulm).
Allergies: benztropine (anticholinergic toxicity); tree/grass/weed pollen.

VS: BP 109/68, HR 63, RR 13, T 36.7, SpO2 94% RA, wt 64.2 kg, BMI 20.0.
Gen: calm, cooperative, NAD.
Skin: normal color, not flushed, normal moisture.
HEENT: pupils equal, normal size, briskly reactive. Mucous membranes moist. Mild bilateral ptosis as before.
CV: RRR, no murmur.
Lungs: mildly prolonged expiration, otherwise clear.
Abd: soft, NT.
Neuro: alert, oriented to person, place, date and situation. Attention normal. No tremor or rigidity. Mild proximal weakness unchanged.

A/P:
1. Anticholinergic toxicity from benztropine: resolved. Benztropine on allergy list; he and psychiatry are aware not to restart it.
2. Schizophrenia, new dx 6/2026: on risperidone 2 mg daily, continuing per psychiatry, who are following him. Med rec done with him today.
3. Risperidone metabolic monitoring: fasting glucose or A1c, lipids and weight at a follow-up in September; lab order placed.
4. AATD with emphysema on weekly augmentation, mitochondrial myopathy, allergic rhinitis: stable, no changes. Yearly neurology review is due; he will book it.
TCM: discharge records reviewed, med reconciliation, interactive contact 7/6.
RTC September (fasting).

documents.title: After Visit Summary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after your hospital stay and ED visit.

Medicines:
- Keep taking risperidone 2 mg once a day as prescribed by psychiatry.
- Do NOT take benztropine. It is now listed as an allergy in your chart.
- Cetirizine, fluticasone spray, allergy shots, albuterol inhaler and weekly augmentation infusions: no change.

Next visit: September, fasting, for blood sugar, cholesterol and weight checks that go with risperidone.
Keep your psychiatry appointments.
Call or text us right away for fever, confusion, blurry vision or trouble eating or drinking.
